html:
On 15 August 1975 a group of junior army officers stormed the house of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding president of Bangladesh, on Road 32 in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, and killed him and most of his family.

Mujib had led the country to independence in the 1971 war, but his rule had turned troubled. The famine of 1974 and corruption cost him support, and early in 1975 he made the Awami League the only legal party. The killers, angry officers, set up a new government and passed a law shielding themselves from trial.

Two daughters survived because they were abroad. One, Sheikh Hasina, later led the Awami League. Coups followed in November 1975, and General Ziaur Rahman rose to power, starting years of military rule. The indemnity law was repealed in 1996, and five of the killers were hanged in 2010.
sum: On 15 August 1975 a group of junior army officers stormed the house of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the founding president of Bangladesh, on Road 32 in Dhanmondi, Dhaka, and killed him and most of his family.
